content.problemStatement: Build a minimal, internet-safe URL shortener as a Spring Boot 3 / Java 21 HTTP service: create a short code for an absolute http(s) URL, redirect visitors of the short code to the original URL while counting the click, expose per-link click statistics, and provide a health endpoint. v0 runs locally with no external dependencies; persistence is in-memory behind a storage port so a JDBC store can be added without touching the HTTP layer.

functionalRequirements.text: POST /api/links with {url} returns 201 with a 7-character base62 code and the full short URL.
GET /:code redirects (302) to the original URL and records a click.
GET /api/links/:code/stats returns the click count and last click time.
Only absolute http/https URLs are accepted; anything else is a 400.
Unknown codes return 404 on redirect and stats.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Codes are random (not sequential) so links cannot be enumerated.
Redirects use 302 with Cache-Control: no-store so every click is counted.
Runs with `mvn spring-boot:run`; no database or container required for v0.
Storage is behind an interface with a contract test so a durable adapter can be added later.

acceptanceCriteria.then: 201 with a 7-char base62 code and shortUrl = baseUrl/code

acceptanceCriteria.given: javascript:, ftp:, malformed or empty URL

acceptanceCriteria.then: 200 with clicks=2 and a lastClickAt timestamp

assumptions: No authentication in v0; anyone can create links (rate limiting is a v1 concern and is noted as a risk).
'How many times clicked' means a total count plus last click time; referrer/UA breakdowns are v1.
'Safe to expose' means: scheme allowlist on targets, random codes, no caching of redirects, schema-validated input.
In-memory persistence is acceptable for v0 as long as the storage port makes replacement straightforward.

ambiguities.question: What does 'how many times each link was clicked' need to include?

options.description: Total clicks and last click time
options.impact: Trivial in-memory counter; enough for v0.
Requires an event log and aggregation; better as v1 once storage is durable.

ambiguities.resolution: count+last for v0; breakdowns tracked as a follow-up.

ambiguities.question: Does 'safe to expose on the internet' require rate limiting in v0?

options.description: Input validation and random codes only
options.impact: Ships faster; abuse control added with durable storage.

options.description: Per-IP rate limiting on the create endpoint
options.impact: One more dependency and config surface.

ambiguities.resolution: Not in v0; recorded as a risk with a mitigation plan.

risks.mitigation: Scheme allowlist now; denylist/reputation checks and rate limiting in v1.

risks.risk: In-memory store loses data on restart.
risks.mitigation: Documented v0 limitation; storage port + contract test make SQLite/Postgres a contained change.

risks.risk: Code collisions as the keyspace fills.
risks.mitigation: 62^7 keys, collision check with bounded retry.
